hazard: w:gridSpan in the HEADER row of a 5-column grid, plus a w:vMerge row group. The frozen corpus's only gridSpan is on a trailing full-width row, so the case that shifts every column label is untested there.
truth: cell start coordinates reflect gridSpan/vMerge structure exactly; WordprocessingML supplies no semantic row/column-header relation, so none is invented.

probes.why: the spanned first row advances the answer to exact grid column 3 without inventing a semantic header
the following answer is grid column 4, not physical cell-array position 3
the last grid column is retained rather than dropped
WordprocessingML has no th/scope equivalent; a confident semantic label would be an unsupported fact
adjacency to a vertically merged cell does not establish semantic row-header scope
the explicit restart-cell text remains addressable at its own coordinate
the continuation row's explicit cell text remains at its structural coordinate

hazard: w:gridBefore — a row that starts part-way across the grid. Absent from the frozen corpus entirely; the one table case where docling beats both mammoth and the deployed parser.
truth: row 3 skips grid column 1, so its cells begin at grid columns 2 and 3; no semantic header is inferred.

probes.why: the row declares one skipped column, so its first cell is grid column 2
and its second is grid column 3
reading the row as if it began at column 1 files an awareness answer under the brand-name column
the same shift on the next cell — mammoth gets this one wrong too

hazard: w:ruby — the phonetic reading (w:rt) and the word (w:rubyBase) are BOTH w:t runs, so a flat run scan interleaves them.
truth: Q17. 電気の契約について。

probes.text: Q17. 電気の契約について。
probes.why: the sentence a reader sees, byte-exact
the visible phonetic annotation is retained as a separate, non-inline source block
the second reading is independently addressable without corrupting the base sentence

hazard: w:listItem shapes the frozen corpus hides: Word's DEFAULT w:value == w:displayText, an item with NO w:displayText, and numeric values (the shape that makes a value-as-code rule look correct).
truth: the options are exactly the displayed strings, and the document prints no code for any of them.

probes.why: one (list) line per listItem is the shape extract/expand.ts#parseDocumentedOptions reads correctly; a single joined blob is not
w:displayText is optional; an item without one displays its w:value, and dropping such an item is a silent loss of a real answer option
the label is the display text, never the value

what a value-as-code rule emits on Word's DEFAULT document. CODED_OPTION would not match it, so the doubled string seals AS THE LABEL — a label the document never printed, hunted for on a live screen where it can never appear
w:value is a stored value, never a rendered one. Minting it as the answer CODE is the same defect this parser already refuses for Word auto-numbering, where it prints [#] instead
the host paragraph before the inline control is untouched — the options are ADDED, never substituted
and the text after it, the classic truncation victim

hazard: a dropdown content control at BLOCK level: its w:sdtPr sits outside every w:p, where the per-paragraph option scan cannot reach it.
truth: the control's own content is extracted; its OPTIONS are not, and the parser must say so in coverage.problems rather than go quiet. The named coverage problem is asserted in worker-v2/tools/tests/docx-robustness.test.mjs, which can see the coverage object; a text probe cannot.

probes.text: Q30. Which zone are you in?
probes.why: the paragraph before a block-level control must survive it
the control's own sdtContent is a normal paragraph and is read normally

hazard: a non-leading w:tblHeader flag is invalid repeat-on-page metadata, not a semantic header declaration. Treating it as th/scope invents relations WordprocessingML never encoded.
truth: all cells retain structural coordinates; rowHeader/colHeader stay null and the late repeat flag is reported.

probes.why: repeat-on-page does not establish semantic scope
the next cell likewise carries no invented semantic label
guess row 0 and every answer in the table is labelled with the TABLE'S TITLE as its column header — a fact about the cell that is not true of it
a full-width title row belongs to no single column and carries no row label

hazard: 886 bytes declaring w:gridSpan w:val="99999999". Column headers are mapped ONE GRID COLUMN AT A TIME, so an unbounded span is a CPU/memory kill inside a Worker from a document small enough to arrive by email.
truth: the document is read, and no coordinate runs away.

probes.text: Q40. Ordinary question above a hostile table.
probes.why: a hostile table must not take the rest of the document down with it
the spanning cell is still read

the span is clamped (MAX_GRID_COLUMNS), so no cell claims a five-digit grid column. Same class of guard as MAX_TAG_SCANS, and the same reason: an 18.5-second scan of a 98 KB upload is a kill, not a slow parse
the body row survives at its exact start coordinate without an invented header relation
